A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PNKA, with matching authors, core equations, proofs and retained experiments despite the changed title and research emphasis. Their text, tables, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original trained-model comparisons, image perturbation experiments, neuron-selection probes and analyses of word embeddings.

after.justification: v2 retains original representation-similarity experiments and reports new COMPAS/Adult fairness audits and contextual-embedding analyses.

M1.justification: PNKA retains column-centered representations, kernel similarity matrices and cosine comparison of corresponding rows, with optional averaging across points. RBF kernels were already permitted in v1; the new audits and removed applications do not alter the core algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds COMPAS recidivism and Adult income tasks, auditing race and gender respectively, plus contextual embeddings on SEAT-7/8. CIFAR-10/100 remain for similarity checks and SemBias remains for static embeddings. The perturbed-image scenarios and neuron-interpretability task are removed.

E2.justification: The interpretability comparisons against activation-based and random neuron selection disappear with v1 Section 5/Appendix D. The direct-cosine comparison on SemBias also disappears (v1 Figure 23), although cosine remains in neighborhood comparisons. CKA comparisons remain; newly audited debiasing models are not themselves competing PNKA metrics.

E3.justification: v2 introduces utility-only versus fairness-objective controls, lowest-10% subgroup audits, and downstream accuracy, statistical-parity, consistency, precision and recall evaluation. It adds RBF-kernel evaluations and revises the stated gender-projection calculation. These establish new protocols and a reported metric revision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1's prediction-disagreement, misclassification, blur/elastic/PGD perturbation and neuron-removal analyses are removed. v2 adds kernel-sensitivity checks, demographic characterization of strongly affected individuals, downstream validation of fairness hypotheses and an alternative contextual gender-direction analysis. Neighborhood-overlap checks are largely retained.

E5.justification: The explicit seed identifiers 0–5 and per-seed reporting in v1 Appendix A/Table 2 are removed. Retained neighborhood and CKA/PNKA comparisons still report three runs, with unchanged uncertainty values in Table 3. The new fairness audits do not add repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial tabular and contextual results while removing v1's error, perturbation and neuron results. For example, new Table 2 reports COMPAS Caucasian precision of 0.6797 versus 0.5465 and Adult female recall of 0.0752 versus 0.4146 for utility-only versus group-fairness representations. These are new comparisons, not version-to-version gains. Table 3 and the SemBias scores in v1 Table 5/v2 Table 4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix E.2 defines nonnegative projection magnitudes using an unnormalized gender vector; v2 Section 4.3 instead defines signed projections onto a normalized direction and uses the absolute baseline projection in the denominator. This changes the mathematical definition of the diagnostic. PNKA's definition and invariance proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion shift from a general similarity measure supporting misclassification analysis, neuron interpretation and interventions to a fairness-auditing framework. v2 adds central claims about contrasting group/individual fairness effects, predicting downstream demographic outcomes and diagnosing contextual debiasing failures; the misclassification and neuron contributions are dropped.

C2.justification: v2 adds reasoning linking representation changes to less favorable COMPAS outcomes for Caucasians and more favorable Adult outcomes for females, and interprets small contextual gender shifts as ineffective debiasing. v1's OOD and neuron-specialization interpretations disappear. The static-embedding amplification explanation remains, while the earlier limited-model/penultimate-layer limitation is omitted.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix A's SGD hyperparameters, 150-epoch checkpoint selection and A40/A100 resource information disappear despite retained CIFAR experiments. v2 adds an AIF360 preprocessing reference, the albert-base-v2 checkpoint and last-layer CLS extraction details. This substantially changes reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to retained training settings.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands fairness and debiasing literature and revises novelty positioning. Section 5 explicitly acknowledges Moschella et al. (2022) as proposing a resembling pointwise measure, distinguishing fairness auditing from model stitching. Much of v1's interpretability, calibration and CKA-sensitivity discussion is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and closing discussion are extensively rewritten around fairness auditing. General properties are compressed into Section 2.3, related work moves into an expanded later section, and the retained word-embedding material is reorganized into evaluation, hypothesis and validation subsections.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the prediction, perturbation and neuron displays with tabular fairness distributions, subgroup tables, demographic ring charts and contextual-embedding plots. Retained displays are resized and relocated, and captions are revised. The TMLR template also changes the author block, headings, headers and table-caption placement.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the fairness application by testing subgroup hypotheses against downstream outcomes (Tables 1–2), extending audits to contextual embeddings and acknowledging closely related pointwise work. However, it removes training details needed for retained experiments, and the new tabular section contains contradictory descriptions of statistical parity and logistic versus linear regression (Section 3.3 and table captions). These concrete gains and reproducibility/reporting costs leave the net quality change uncertain.
